These thoughts stayed with me but I was never particularly interested in Politics or Law.

This recipe requires a bit of work and might seem complicated, but it is totally worth it! We want a smooth, dense cheesecake, not a lumpy fluffy one, so there are important hints regarding the creamcheese and eggs in the recipe that follows.

Ingredients (not including the blueberry topping): 4 cream cheese, softened, 12oz ea. (48 ounces total at room temperature); 1 and 1/4 cup sugar; 4 tbsp all-purpose flour; 4 eggs; 1/4 cup sour cream; 1/4 cup heavy cream; 2 eggs yolks; 1 tsp vanilla extract; 1 tsp almond extract.

Directions: I use a pre-made mix for the graham cracker crust; this is usually just course graham cracker flour, butter, and sugar. You can find these in the cake section of your grocery store or find a recipe on the internet. Press the graham cracker crust mix, made according to directions on the box, firmly into the bottom of a 9” springform pan. Bake the pan with the crust at 325°F for ten minutes, cool, then refrigerate until needed. •When you do this, the crust will brown a just little bit.

Preheat oven to 325°F. Position rack in center of oven. With mixer at high speed beat the hell out of the cream cheese until smooth, at least 8 minutes. Combine the sugar and flour. Reduce mixer speed to low; beat sugar mixture into cream cheese, 1/4 cup at a time until smooth, about 5 minutes. •You will have a smooth cheesecake if the cream cheese has been thoroughly beaten and you really can’t overbeat the creamcheese, so beat it to death. In a second bowl very gently stir together eggs, sour cream, heavy cream, yolks and vanilla and almond extract. Do NOT beat the egg mixture, just gently mix it until all of the yolks are broken and it has a mostly uniform consistency. •If you beat the egg mixture, air will be incorporated into it and the cheesecake will end up being fluffy, rather than dense. To belabor the point: very gently stir the eggs, sour cream, heavy cream, yolks and vanilla and almond extract together. Gradually add the egg mixture to the cream cheese mixture and gently stir until just the two are just incorporated. Butter the sides of the springform pan. Wrap outside of the pan with a double layer of heavy-duty foil. Pour the batter into a springform pan. •For some reason, I tend to forget to butter the sides of the pan at this point. If you want a beautiful looking cake, remember to butter the sides of the pan. Place the aluminum wrapped springform pan into a larger baking pan and fill the outer pan with water until it is halfway up the sides of the wrapped springform pan. Bake 1 1/2 hours. •The cheesecake may not seem like it's done, but it is. Don’t overcook it! Remove from water bath and remove the foil. Cool on a wire rack then place your cake into a refrigerator for at least 3 hours (or over night).

Blueberry topping: Add 3 cups of frozen blueberries to a pot with 1/8 cup sugar; 1/8 cup water; and ¼ teaspoon salt. Bring mixture to a slow boil for 10 minutes; stir frequently. Remove from heat and let it cool uncovered. •The topping may seem liquidy, but that’s part of the magic. When you put this topping on your cheesecake the blueberry liquid will be absorbed by the cheesecake as it cools. It will give a blueberry marbled effect within the cake with lots of scrumptious blueberries on top.
